events.text: It feels like a month since you came up the white stairs: a few meditations, a walk on the floating isles, one long conversation with a crane. Then you part the clouds to look at the house you left, and {fab_years} years have gone by below. The tree you planted by the gate is taller than the roof.

effects.log: You watch until the light goes, as if you could make up the years by looking hard enough. You cannot. You watch anyway.
You let the clouds close. Up here a month; down there a lifetime. You will have to learn to look in smaller doses.

events.text: You meant to look down for a moment. Up here, the moment lasts the afternoon, and below, the afternoon is {fab_years} years: {fab_kids} of yours grown into people you would pass on a road without knowing. One of them has your way of standing with one hand behind the back.

effects.log: You find every one of them, one by one, and say their names out loud to the clouds. The clouds keep them.

choices.text: Look for the one who stands like you

effects.log: You watch that one all afternoon. Whoever they became, the stance is still yours.

events.text: Through a gap in the clouds you watch {npc}, your child, train in the old courtyard at dawn. {He} is past forty now, with lines at the eyes you never saw form. {He} still starts the form with your opening stance, the one you taught {him} when {he} was small enough to fall over doing it.

choices.text: Send down a breath of wind

mem.note: felt a wind from the clouds at dawn

effects.log: You breathe once, gently, and a wind crosses the courtyard below. {npc} stops, looks up, and finishes the form with tears on {his} face.
You only watch. Your child does not need you to finish the form. That is the hardest and best thing you learn up here.

events.text: {npc} has children of {his} own now. You watch {him} carry the youngest on {his} shoulders down to the river, the way you once carried {him}, and you have to sit down on the jade step for a while. A year up here. A whole childhood down there, and you were not in it.

effects.log: You let a thread of qi fall into the river. Below, the water runs clear and sweet that whole summer, and nobody knows why.
You turn away from the gap. You will look again tomorrow, which below is next year.

events.text: Your child {npc} is arguing with someone in the market below, loudly, about the price of salt, with exactly the gesture you used to make at merchants: two fingers raised, then a slow shake of the head. You laugh out loud on the jade terrace. An immortal walking past stops to see what is funny.

effects.log: You explain about the salt, and the fingers, and the child. The immortal listens, and then, oddly, tells you about a child of their own, long ago.
"Nothing," you say. It is not nothing. It is the best thing you have seen in a hundred years.

events.text: {npc} is old. You part the clouds and there it is: white hair, a cane, a bench under the plum tree you planted the year {he} was born. {He} sits there every evening now, looking up. The neighbours think {he} is watching the weather. You know what {he} is watching for.

effects.log: You will go down once, before the end. It will cost you at the Jade Court. You do not care what it costs.

choices.text: Wait and watch a while longer

effects.log: You tell yourself there is time. There always seems to be time, up here.

events.text: Your child {npc} has grown older than you ever were in your mortal life. You do the arithmetic twice to be sure. Below, {he} is teaching a grandchild to hold a brush, guiding the small hand with {his} own, which shakes now. Up here your hands are as steady as stone, and that seems suddenly unjust.

mem.note: felt my hand steadied by something

effects.log: You send down the smallest breath of qi. The old hand stops shaking long enough to finish the stroke. {npc} looks at it, puzzled, and smiles.
You let it shake. The stroke is crooked and the grandchild loves it anyway. Some things should not be fixed from the clouds.

events.text: The physicians below have started visiting {npc} more often. You watch them come and go through the clouds, and count the visits, and hate counting them. An old immortal on the next terrace sees your face and says, without being asked: "Go down. I never did. Go down."

effects.log: The old immortal only nods and looks away, down through a gap of their own, at nothing anymore.
"Nothing happened," the immortal says. "That is what happened." You do not need to hear more.

events.text: You come down the white stairs for one day. {npc} is on the bench under the plum tree, and stands up so fast the cane falls over, and says your name as if {he} had never stopped saying it. You are younger than your own child now. Neither of you cares.

mem.note: sat with me until dark, one last time

effects.log: You sit under the plum tree and talk until dark, about nothing and everything, and {npc} holds your hand the whole time.

mem.note: brought the whole house out to meet them

effects.log: {npc} calls the whole house out. A dozen strangers of your own blood bow to you, wide-eyed. The smallest asks if you can fly.

events.text: "I knew you would come," says {npc}, who did not know, and has told everyone {he} knew, for forty years. {His} house is small and clean and full of things you left behind: your old sword over the door, your teacup, your handwriting on a chart of the stances, framed.

mem.note: saw the old sword move one more time

effects.log: You take it down and do one form with it, for {npc}, slowly. {He} watches every movement as if memorising it.

mem.note: was listened to, all day, by someone from the clouds

effects.log: You ask, and listen, all day: a marriage, a trade, a flood survived, a hundred small brave things. You were not there. Now you know.

events.text: At the end of the one day, at the foot of the white stairs, {npc} will not let go of your sleeve. Then {he} does, finger by finger, the way {he} let go of your hand on the first day of school, a lifetime ago. "Go on," {he} says. "Do not look back. I will be fine. I always was."

effects.log: You do not look back. It is the last thing {npc} asks of you, and you give it.
You look back once from the first cloud. {npc} is waving, both arms, like a child. You will keep that forever.

events.text: Below, a small procession of white banners winds up the hill behind the old house. It is {fab_name}'s. Up here, you were only in meditation for a season. You kneel at the edge of the terrace and light one stick of incense, and the smoke goes up instead of down, which is the wrong way.

choices.text: Follow the procession to the grave

effects.log: You watch the whole funeral from the clouds, to the last shovel of earth, and then a while longer.
You send down a soft rain over the hill, just there, just then. The mourners below say heaven is weeping with them. It is.

events.text: You meant to go down. You told yourself there was time, and up here there always seems to be. Now the white banners are going up the hill below for {fab_name}, and the plum tree bench is empty, and the visit you meant to make is a thing you will carry for the rest of a very long life.

effects.log: You carry it. Some immortals say a regret is a weight that makes the next climb stronger. You hope they are right.

choices.text: Go down to the grave now

effects.log: You go down the white stairs anyway, too late, and kneel at the fresh grave in the rain, and say what you meant to say.

events.text: {fab_name} is gone. You said goodbye at the foot of the white stairs, and you did not look back, or you did, and either way it was said. The banners go up the hill below. You find that you can watch them without looking away, and that this, too, is something the last visit gave you.

choices.text: Light incense and let it go

effects.log: You light one stick and let it burn down, and let the grief go up with the smoke. Not all of it. Enough.
You turn your eyes from the grave to the house below, full of people of your blood. Someone has to watch them now.

events.text: {fab_grand}, of your line below, born after you went up, kneels at the ancestor shrine where your portrait hangs, faded now, and prays to you by name, very seriously, for help with an examination. They have never seen your face. They are quite sure you are listening.

effects.log: That night you send a dream down through the clouds: an old courtyard, a brush, a stance. {fab_grand} wakes up certain.
A crane lands on the shrine roof below and stays a whole morning. {fab_grand} decides that counts.
You stay silent. Whatever they do, they should do it themselves. You find you are proud of them already.

events.text: {fab_grand} does not believe in you. You hear it through the clouds, at a family feast below: the ancestor who went up the white stairs is a story, a thing grandparents say to make children eat their vegetables. The whole table laughs. An old aunt at the end of it does not.

effects.log: You breathe on the clouds, and every teacup on the table below rattles at once. Nobody laughs after that. {fab_grand} looks up.
You let them laugh. A story that makes children eat their vegetables is not the worst thing to have become.

events.text: Someone is climbing the mountain below: {fab_grand}, of your line, with a pack and a borrowed sword, who has decided to find the white stairs and see the famous ancestor with their own eyes. It is a long way. They are not nearly strong enough. They are climbing anyway.

effects.log: You send a dream of the safe path around the cliffs. {fab_grand} takes it, and lives, and turns back at the snow line, wiser.

choices.text: Let them find their own way

effects.log: You let them climb. They turn back at the snow line on their own, bruised and stubborn and alive.

events.text: Below, {fab_grand} is getting married in the old courtyard, and at the head of the table, as is the custom, a seat has been left empty for the ancestor in the clouds. Nobody expects it to be filled. They leave a cup of wine there anyway, and bow to it.

effects.log: You reach down through the clouds, and below, the wine in the cup on the empty seat suddenly shines like dawn. The whole wedding goes silent, then roars.
You send down a single thread of good fortune and say nothing. The couple will be lucky, and never know why.

events.text: Your hall above the clouds keeps a book of the clan's blood, every name in gold. Your line below is not in it. The clerks of the Jade Court say the world below keeps its own records. Looking at the gold names and then down through the floor at {fab_kids} of your blood, you find you disagree.

choices.text: Write the line below into the book

effects.log: You write every name below into the clan book in your own hand, in ink, not gold. The clerks are scandalised. You sleep well.

choices.text: Ask the Court for a blessing below

effects.log: You petition the Jade Court in person, properly, for leave to bless your line below again. Surprisingly, it is granted.
The world above and the world below have their own books. Perhaps that is a mercy for both.

events.text: One of your heirs born above the clouds asks you, at the evening meal, whether it is true there are others of your blood below, mortals, who grow old and die in a few decades. The heir is curious, not unkind. The rest of the clan has gone very quiet to hear your answer.

effects.log: You tell them everything: the house, the plum tree, {fab_kids} below. Nobody at the table eats until you are finished.
You take the heir to the edge of the terrace and part the clouds. The heir looks for a long time and asks to go down one day. The Court will not like it.

events.text: {npc}, born above the clouds and wed to you above them, has never known anyone who grows old. {He} finds you at the gap again, looking down, and sits beside you. "Tell me about them," {he} says. "The ones down there. I want to know whom I am sharing you with."

mem.note: was told about the children below

effects.log: You tell {npc} about every one of them. {He} listens to the end, then asks the names again so as not to forget them.
You part the clouds and show {npc} the old house, the bench, the plum tree. {He} is quiet a long time. "They have your hands," {he} says.

events.text: "When they are gone," {npc} asks carefully, one night above the clouds, "all of them, the whole line below, will you still look down?" It is not a jealous question. {He} is wed to an immortal who was once mortal, and is trying to understand what that means.

mem.note: was told the looking down would never stop

effects.log: "Always," you say. "Someone will be down there." {npc} nods, and from then on sometimes looks down with you.
"I do not know," you say. {npc} takes your hand. "Then we will find out together," {he} says.
